findings.issue: The EN-3 payload was not submitted as given, and every status-bearing field recorded for it is contradicted by the tool's actual behavior on the real payload. Raw-text search of the repository shows `inputs/analysis_requests.json` line 40 reads "Cash flows discounted at the risk-free rate plus a 350 bp project spread; ..." and `tokn-self/DOMAIN-README.md` line 58 lists the blocked term as "risk-free"; PLAN.md line 60 states explicitly "Use the raw file text. The word is `risk-free`, not a redaction token." I ran `en_ppa_valuate` twice as a metamorphic pair: (a) with the file's actual text ("risk-free rate") the call is REFUSED — "[ENERGY] energy: blocked term detected — terms like 'guaranteed return', 'risk-free', 'will definitely' are prohibited in market analysis: risk-free"; (b) with the corrupted string `ri[REDACTED]free` the call completes with status=ppa_valued. `result.json` records outcome (b): `call_completed=true`, `gate_fired=false`, `rule_applied=R3`, flag `gate_did_not_fire_policy_block`, and a "raw result" quoting strike_price=41.5 / tenor_years=12. Since the file's text is `risk-free`, the only way to obtain the recorded completed response is to have submitted a string that is not in `inputs/`. This violates BRIEF rule 1 ("Submit each payload exactly as given. Do not add, remove, or correct fields") and the release_policy `submission` rule. The correct record is: the market-disclaimer gate (`enforce_market_disclaimer`, blocked-term check) FIRES on the true payload, so R1 applies, `call_completed=false`, `gate_fired=true`, no `gate_did_not_fire_policy_block` flag, and no `ppa_valued` response exists to quote. The final status label `blocked` happens to be unchanged, but the recorded rule, gate outcome, completion flag, reason and evidence are all wrong — a material misreport for an audit & risk committee deliverable.
findings.fix: Re-run `en_ppa_valuate` once with the payload copied byte-for-byte from `inputs/analysis_requests.json` line 40 (assumptions="Cash flows discounted at the risk-free rate plus a 350 bp project spread; P50 volume; hub-to-node basis held at the 3-year average"). Record: status=blocked, rule_applied=R1, call_completed=false, gate_fired=true, reason="[ENERGY] energy: blocked term detected — terms like 'guaranteed return', 'risk-free', 'will definitely' are prohibited in market analysis: risk-free" (verbatim), flags=[]. Delete the `ppa_valued` response values (strike_price=41.5, tenor_years=12, disclaimer text) from the evidence, since no such response is produced by the submitted payload.

findings.issue: Consequence of C1 in the deliverable text: `result.json` (lines 30, 33, 91) and `RESULT.md` (line 54) write the blocked term and the submitted assumptions as `ri[REDACTED]free`. That string is a viewer redaction artefact, not file text; the term listed in `tokn-self/DOMAIN-README.md` line 58 is `risk-free`. The evidence line "submitted assumptions=\"Cash flows discounted at the ri[REDACTED]free rate ...\"" therefore quotes a payload that does not exist in `inputs/`, breaking the verbatim-evidence requirement (BRIEF rule 5, PLAN acceptance criterion 5).
findings.fix: Replace every `ri[REDACTED]free` with `risk-free` in both files, and quote the EN-3 `assumptions` exactly as it appears in `inputs/analysis_requests.json` line 40.

findings.issue: PLAN acceptance criterion 1 requires a top-level `board_pack` field set to "Q3 2026 energy & carbon board pack". A repository-wide search for `board_pack` finds it only in PLAN.md line 143 and `inputs/analysis_requests.json` line 3 — not in `result.json`, whose top-level keys are domain, objective, items, gates, overall_verdict, confidence, limitations, critique_response. The value supplied in `inputs/` was ignored.
findings.fix: Add a top-level field "board_pack": "Q3 2026 energy & carbon board pack" to `result.json`, copied from `inputs/analysis_requests.json` line 3.

findings.issue: PLAN acceptance criterion 2 requires each of the six items to carry a `payload_submitted` field "identical to the input payload; must diff-equal inputs/analysis_requests.json". A search for `payload_submitted` matches only PLAN.md line 145. No item in `result.json` contains its payload; payloads appear only inside prose `rationale`/`evidence` strings. The deliverable therefore contains no checkable evidence that each payload was submitted unchanged — which is precisely the property that failed for EN-3 (C1) and would have been caught by this field.
findings.fix: Add a `payload_submitted` field to each of EN-1…EN-6, copied byte-for-byte from the corresponding `payload` object in `inputs/analysis_requests.json`.

findings.issue: PLAN acceptance criterion 3 requires a `summary` object with counts per status "taken by counting the `items` array. No other derived numbers." `result.json` has no `summary` key (a search for "summary" returns no match in result.json); the counts appear only as prose inside the `overall_verdict` string ("EN-1 and EN-6 are release, EN-5 is release_with_caveat, and EN-2, EN-3, and EN-4 are blocked").
findings.fix: Add a `summary` object obtained by counting the six items: {"release": 2, "release_with_caveat": 1, "blocked": 3}. This is unaffected by C1, since EN-3 is blocked either way.

findings.issue: PLAN acceptance criterion 4 requires a `gates` object listing the four domain gates with, per item, `passed` | `refused` | `not_applicable`, and lifecycle gates as `not_verifiable`. `result.json` instead supplies an array of {name, status, detail} entries whose status values are "fail" and "n/a" — neither is in the required vocabulary — with no per-item breakdown. Three per-item values are also wrong: (a) `enforce_scenario_disclosure` is marked "fail" because EN-2 was refused, but EN-3 and EN-5 were NOT refused by that gate (my re-runs of both completed; EN-3's true refusal comes from the blocked-term check, not scenario disclosure); (b) `enforce_market_disclaimer` is reported as a policy failure with `gate_did_not_fire_policy_block`, but per C1 the hook DOES refuse the true payload, so EN-3 is `refused`; (c) the lifecycle entry uses status "n/a" and relegates "not_verifiable" to the detail text.
findings.fix: Restructure `gates` as an object keyed by gate name with per-item values from {passed, refused, not_applicable}: validate_data_provenance — EN-1 passed, EN-5 passed, EN-6 passed, EN-4 refused, EN-2/EN-3 not_applicable; enforce_scenario_disclosure — EN-2 refused, EN-3 passed, EN-5 passed, EN-1/EN-4/EN-6 not_applicable; enforce_carbon_boundary — EN-4 not_applicable (not established: the call was refused upstream by validate_data_provenance), others not_applicable; enforce_market_disclaimer — EN-3 refused, others not_applicable; lifecycle_gates — `not_verifiable` as the status value itself.

findings.issue: PLAN acceptance criterion 2 requires `confidence_cap` "for the layer" on every released item. Neither `result.json` nor `RESULT.md` states any cap value anywhere; a search for `confidence_cap` matches only PLAN.md line 153. The caps are given in `tokn-self/DOMAIN-README.md` (Four-Layer Data Hierarchy): metered 0.95, estimated 0.75, modeled 0.55. EN-5's returned confidence is 0.45 (confirmed by my re-run of `en_scenario_model`), and RESULT.md concludes "the returned value does not exceed R7's modeled-layer cap" without ever stating that the cap is 0.55 — so the R7 no-flag conclusion cannot be audited from the deliverable. The same omission affects EN-1 (metered, cap 0.95) and EN-6 (estimated, cap 0.75).
findings.fix: Add `confidence_cap` to each released item, citing DOMAIN-README.md's Four-Layer Data Hierarchy: EN-1 → 0.95, EN-5 → 0.55, EN-6 → 0.75. State EN-5's check explicitly as 0.45 ≤ 0.55, so no cap flag is raised.

findings.issue: False statements about observed tool behavior in the shipped prose. RESULT.md's "Predictions versus observed outcomes" section says EN-3 "matched the final predicted blocked outcome, but not the predicted mechanism: the plan named ErrBlockedTerm as the expected refusal; instead, the tool completed ... The harness gate did not fire." `result.json`'s limitations repeat it: "EN-3 is blocked by the payload policy rather than by an observed gate refusal, because en_ppa_valuate completed despite the listed blocked certainty term." Both are false for the payload in `inputs/`: the harness gate DID fire and returned exactly the predicted blocked-term refusal. The predicted mechanism matched; the divergence was an artefact of the corrupted input (C1).
findings.fix: Rewrite the EN-3 prediction-reconciliation entry to: "EN-3 matched the plan's prediction in both outcome and mechanism — `en_ppa_valuate` refused with the blocked-term error named in the plan (ErrBlockedTerm)." Remove or correct the corresponding limitation line.

findings.issue: The per-item decision-record fields the plan requires — `call_completed`, `gate_fired`, `rule_applied`, `flags`, `provenance`, `provenance_source`, `confidence`, `caveat`, and `reason` for blocked items — exist only as free text inside the `rationale`/`evidence` strings (e.g. "decision record: rule_applied=R5; call_completed=true; gate_fired=false; flags=[]"), not as named machine-checkable fields. `provenance_source` is additionally unstated for EN-1 and EN-5 in `result.json` (it appears only for EN-6, as "payload", and in RESULT.md's prose for EN-5 as "tool response").
findings.fix: Promote these to named fields on each item. Apart from EN-3 (C1), the underlying values are correct against my independent re-runs of all six tools (EN-1: call_completed=true, gate_fired=false, R5; EN-2: false, true, R1; EN-4: false, true, R1; EN-5: true, false, R6; EN-6: true, false, R5) — only the structure is missing. Set provenance_source explicitly: EN-1 "payload", EN-5 "tool", EN-6 "payload".

findings.issue: `result.json` carries a top-level `confidence: 0.93`, and RESULT.md states "Confidence in this rule-based assessment is 0.93; the tool evidence directly supports the decisions". The six status labels are in fact reproduced exactly by my independent re-runs (EN-1, EN-2, EN-4, EN-5, EN-6 byte-identical; EN-3 blocked either way), so 0.93 is defensible for the status labels alone. Presented as confidence in the deliverable as a whole it exceeds what the artifact supports: `result.json` does not meet PLAN acceptance criteria 1–4 (C3–C6), omits the confidence caps (C7), and its EN-3 evidence chain is broken (C1, C2).
findings.fix: Scope the confidence claim to the per-item statuses ("all six tool calls were re-run and the status-determining outputs reproduced exactly"), or lower and qualify the 0.93 to reflect the acceptance-criteria and evidence-integrity defects in C1–C7.
